title: Bringing God Our First and Best

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Celebrate the Festival of Harvest with the firstfruits of the crops you sow in your field. Celebrate the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your crops from the field." - Exodus 23:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two more festivals marked the seasons of harvest. When the first crops came in, the people celebrated by bringing God the firstfruits — the very first and best of what the land produced. And at the year's end, they gathered again to rejoice over all that had been harvested. These feasts wove gratitude into the rhythm of the seasons, keeping the people mindful that every harvest was a gift from God's hand.

Bringing the firstfruits was an act of faith and worship. It said, "Lord, the first and best belong to You, and I trust You to provide the rest." Rather than clutching everything for themselves, the people opened their hands and gave God the top of the harvest. In doing so, they declared that He was the true source of their provision and the first priority of their hearts.

This challenges us to consider what gets our "firstfruits." Do we give God our best time, energy, and resources, or only our leftovers after everything else is claimed? God invites us to put Him first, trusting that a life which honours Him will not lack (Matt 6:33). And these harvest feasts find a rich fulfilment in Christ, who is called the firstfruits of the resurrection (1 Cor 15:20) — the guarantee of the great harvest of eternal life still to come. What a God, who gives us every harvest and then becomes our harvest Himself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What gets my "firstfruits" — my best time, energy, and resources?
Do I live with a heart of gratitude, seeing my blessings as gifts from God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, every good thing I have comes from Your hand. Teach me to give You my first and best, and fill my heart with gratitude for all You so generously provide. Amen.
